Double Taxation Agreement between Samoa and New Zealand (in force 2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies Amendment Acts 2008, 2018 and 2021; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (Samoa); Terrorism Act 2012 (Samoa); AML/CFT directives and guidance issued by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Central Bank of Samoa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of valid passport of each shareholder, director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of residence (underlying passport issued by the national passport authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (consular legalization only if origin state is not party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank, with notarized signature of the issuing officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter on bank letterhead confirming account conduct and standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution maintaining the applicant's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where required by the registered agent's KYC policy)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registered agent in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional standing and source-of-funds declaration (curriculum vitae or professional reference letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Previous employer or licensed professional firm, with notarized signature

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, Australian DFAT sanctions list and Samoa domestic counter-terrorism designations under the Terrorism Act 2012. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates trigger enhanced due diligence under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval and mandatory filing of suspicious transaction reports with the Samoa FIU. Screening results must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry - International Companies Section, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be expressed in Latin script (English or Samoan alphabet); Chinese characters cannot form part of the registered legal name. A Chinese trading name may be recorded solely as an auxiliary transliteration (pinyin) with the Registrar's prior approval. The name must terminate with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc' or an abbreviation of equivalent effect.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank (prior Central Bank of Samoa authorization required)
Trust, Trustee, Nominee (regulatory consent from MCIL required)
Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance (Central Bank of Samoa authorization required)
Finance, Financial, Securities, Mutual Fund, Fund (regulatory authorization required)
Chartered, Royal, Government, Ministry, State, National (ministerial consent required)
University, College, Institute, Academy (education authority consent required)
Cooperative, Building Society, Friendly Society (registrar restriction)
Samoa, Pacific, Apia (consent required to avoid misleading national or regional implication)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the MCIL Registrar within 14 calendar days of the refusal notice, stating the grounds and attaching any fresh ministerial or sectoral consents; no additional filing fee applies to the appeal of an identical name. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, judicial review may be sought before the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days. A successfully cleared name is reserved for 30 days, and a single 30-day extension may be applied for before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the statutory registered office. Every International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa operated by a licensed registered agent under the International Companies Act 1987; substantive business may be managed remotely, but no virtual address can substitute for the agent's physical office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5-10% annual probability for a Low_Risk_Standard LegalTech SaaS file), but the licensed registered agent and all client due-diligence files are exposed to unannounced on-site examinations by the Registrar and the Samoa FIU; the KYC bundle must therefore be inspection-ready at all times.

Government incorporation filing fee for an International Company (authorized capital up to USD 10,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the country of origin (e.g., China, Hong Kong SAR or New Zealand)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille issuance per document bundle in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the origin jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English translation of Chinese-language supporting documents
International courier (DHL/FedEx) for originals and apostilled documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 4 and 7 (Memorandum and Articles of Association; registration of International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued under Form IC-02 (Application to Register an International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit required. International Company may issue one or more shares, and directors determine consideration for issued shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT (1) the subscribers listed in the Memorandum of Association be and are hereby allotted shares in accordance with the share capital provisions contained therein, and the share register be updated accordingly; (2) the registered office of the Company shall be at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, with the registered agent authorized to accept service of process on the Company's behalf; (3) the following persons be and are hereby appointed as the first directors of the Company until the next annual general meeting, each with full powers under the International Companies Act 1987, as amended; and (4) the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute payment facilitator agreements, and take all steps to maintain the Company's tax-exempt status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-01 requesting a name availability search and reservation. The proposed name must include 'International Company' or the abbreviation 'IC' and must not conflict with any existing registered name in Samoa. Payment of the name reservation fee completed at the time of filing.
required_dossiers: Completed Form IC-01
Name reservation fee payment receipt
Notarized copy of incorporator passport or government-issued ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file a written amendment request or submit an alternative name within five business days. A statutory declaration can be submitted to address similarity concerns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoa Notary Public and registered agent; final review by Samoa Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, expressly limiting the company's objects to offshore business, including cloud document automation, e-signature authentication, and LegalTech SaaS services. The incorporators must execute the charter documents before a notary public, and the licensed registered agent must sign the consent to act.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed and notarized)
Consent to act as director (for each initial director)
Consent to act as registered agent
Notarized subscriber declaration with details of share subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises a pre-registration query concerning document content or legal language, amend the affected clause and resubmit within seven days. If disqualification occurs, appeal to the Registrar within fourteen days with corrected supporting documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Companies Registry, MCIL (online portal or physical counter, Apia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form IC-02 together with the name reservation certificate, executed and notarized Memorandum and Articles, consents from directors and registered agent, and proof of payment of the official state filing fee. The application must declare that the International Company will not carry on business in Samoa other than offshore commercial activity permitted under the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Form IC-02 (Application to Register an International Company)
Name reservation certificate
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Original consents from first directors and registered agent
Official state filing fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On receipt of a query, provide clarifications or additional due diligence documents within fourteen days. If the application lapses, re-submit with a covering explanation and pay the re-filing fee if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation and a sealed copy of the Memorandum and Articles. The company obtains its International Company identification number. Verify all corporate particulars and the registered office address as stated on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued)
Sealed Memorandum and Articles of Association
International Company identification number (ICIN)
Registered agent confirmation of office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical or legal error, submit the certificate and a statutory declaration requesting correction to the Registrar within five business days. The corrected certificate will be reissued upon payment of the rectification fee if any.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Statutory Record Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent and Samoa Companies Registry (notification filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, formally approve the share subscription, adopt the registered office, and confirm the appointments of directors and officers. File the first board resolution and any required disclosure notices in the company's statutory records held by the registered agent. If a tax-exemption certificate is desired, submit the corporate evidence to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (dated and signed)
Statement of compliance with International Companies Act 1987
Registered agent record of registered office and directorship
Evidence of share issuance entries in the share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requests additional governance filings, remedy the default by filing a late submission with a supporting explanation and paying the late penalty. If the resolution is defective, hold an adjourned board meeting and adopt a corrective resolution within ten business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – International Company holds no physical industrial establishment or regulated commercial operation in Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required for a cloud-based LegalTech SaaS and e-signature authentication business operated offshore

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – digital professional services; no physical development or industrial activity (Category 5 registration exemption for ICT and knowledge-based services)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – zero wastewater, VOC emissions, or regulated waste generation arising from cloud document automation and electronic signature processing

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable at formation stage. If a physical office is subsequently established in Samoa, a fire safety clearance from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority and an occupational health inspection under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2010 will be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue of Samoa (Maota o Lafi o Tupe), via the Samoa Ministry of Revenue Taxpayer Portal at https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company must apply for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) using Ministry of Revenue Form TIN-001. The application requires the Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar of International Companies, a certified copy of the director's passport, a letter of consent from the registered agent in Samoa, proof of registered office address, and the relevant registration fees. The Director of Revenue issues the TIN within 5–10 working days. The TIN is also the VAT identification number and is prerequisite for VAGST registration, customs operations, and tax return filings. A branch of a foreign entity must additionally submit a Certificate of Registration from the Companies Office and nominate an authorised local representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a check-the-box classification regime. A Samoa International Company is treated as a separate legal person liable to tax only as expressly provided under the International Companies Act 1987 and the Income Tax Ordinance, and it enjoys an exemption from Samoan income tax, withholding tax, and capital gains tax. The only practical election is the voluntary registration for Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) when taxable supplies are made in Samoa or to Samoan residents, which is irrevocable for a minimum period under the VAGST Act. Samoa has no hybrid mismatch election mechanism; however, the Commissioner may reclassify a corporate resident under controlled foreign company or General Anti-Avoidance Rules provisions where a Samoa IC is used to gain inconsistent tax outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 50,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; exemption for an International Company that makes no taxable supplies in Samoa
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa has not yet implemented a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or an API-based e-invoicing system. A VAGST-registered person must issue serially numbered tax invoices containing the supplier's TIN, VAGST registration number, full description of supply, tax amount, and issue date. Electronic invoicing via approved software is accepted if the invoice can be reproduced and audited in readable form. Tax returns and payments are filed electronically through the Ministry of Revenue portal. No digital stamping or government pre-clearance of invoices is currently mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the VAGST Act for (i) commodities physically exported from Samoa under customs control, (ii) services supplied directly to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply and where the benefit of the service is received outside Samoa, and (iii) the supply of goods or services connected to international transport. A Samoa International Company providing legal contract automation SaaS and e-signature authentication must document the non-resident status of the customer, the offshore place of effective use, and the absence of any Samoan consumption. Retention of the signed master SaaS agreement, IP geolocation records of customers, billing address details, payment remittances, and evidence that the customer did not execute contracts in Samoa is necessary to substantiate the zero rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment evidence
Commercial invoice and signed service contract evidencing offshore delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry of Revenue has the authority to audit export zero-rating claims within the statutory timeframe and, if substantiation is insufficient or a transaction is deemed mischaracterised, may retrospectively assess VAGST at 15% on the full supply value, impose late payment penalties and interest, and apply a civil penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall in cases of fraudulent or wilful misdeclaration. A successful clawback can also result in the revocation of exporter zero-rating privileges, publication of the taxpayer's default status, and referral for criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act with fines of up to SAT 50,000 and imprisonment not exceeding 2 years for knowingly participating in an evasion scheme.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), acting as the sole exchange control authority under the Foreign Exchange Control Act and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, with day-to-day supervisory and approval powers delegated to licensed commercial banks operating in Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is not a fully convertible offshore currency. Current account payments related to trade in goods and services are generally permitted without CBS pre-approval, provided a licensed bank verifies underlying documentation. Capital account transfers, including shareholder loans, capital injections, and outward portfolio investments by residents, require CBS permission or a commercial bank's delegated approval. Profit remittance by an International Company (IC) is treated favourably where all revenue is derived from outside Samoa and the IC has no domestic business activity; remittances are typically processed through the local banking system subject to tax clearance and compliance with anti-money laundering requirements. The primary practical hurdle is the unavailability of a deep offshore WST market, so most cross-border treasury flows are denominated in USD or AUD and require concluding FX transactions with the licensed bank as principal.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa does not impose a blanket 100% surrender requirement on export proceeds for International Companies. However, all payments received in foreign currency by a Samoa IC conducting domestic business must be repatriated into Samoa through a licensed authorised dealer within 30 days of receipt. For a pure offshore IC engaged in cross-border LegalTech SaaS subscriptions, no mandatory conversion into WST is required provided the proceeds are booked offshore and not remitted into Samoa's domestic financial system. If the IC voluntarily credits USD proceeds to a local foreign-currency account, the bank will require the underlying SaaS contract and invoices for credit, and conversion into WST will only occur upon explicit instruction for a permitted transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low Feasibility. Samoa has no statutory licensing regime for digital banks, electronic money institutions (EMIs), or non-bank payment processors. Offshore digital EMIs such as Mercury, Airwallex, or Wise are not authorised to open WST-denominated accounts or provide direct Samoa IBAN/routing rails for CBS-regulated transactions. A Samoa IC can only use such EMIs as ancillary receivable-collection gateways for non-Samoa customers, but the EMIs commonly reject offshore company types with no local operating substance unless the IC provides a professional legal opinion, registered agent certification, and evidence of beneficial ownership. The primary operating account should therefore remain with a tier-1 Samoa licensed bank, with the offshore EMI treated merely as a sub-ledger for specific inbound card payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not mandatory for a director of a Samoa International Company. Licensed banks uniformly accept remote corporate account opening where: (i) the director provides a certified ID copy and proof of residential address; (ii) the director undergoes a live video interview conducted by the bank's compliance officer; and (iii) the registered agent certifies the constitutional documents. Physical board representation is only required for the completion of the signatory card at a few institutions, but a power of attorney authorising a local attorney-in-fact to sign bank forms is widely accepted. For the LegalTech SaaS entity, a videoconference interview will suffice, but the final account authorisation normally requires a scanned board resolution and certified passport copy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore company with no commercial presence or employees in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, current Register of Directors and Shareholders, registered agent's Certificate of Good Standing, audited or management financial statements for the last two years, and a notarised board resolution authorising account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth / source of funds for initial share capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank references from the ultimate beneficial owner's primary lending institution, latest personal tax returns or wealth statement, legal source of funds declaration, and a certified copy of the sales contracts or pre-paid subscription agreements supporting the formation capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk e-commerce / SaaS cross-border receivables including credit cards
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial description of the cloud document automation platform, jurisdiction-neutral privacy policy, standard terms of service, PCI-DSS compliance attestation, and a three-month transaction forecast broken down by customer jurisdiction to demonstrate the non-face-to-face, low-risk nature of the business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctions or politically exposed persons (PEPs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP status declaration for each beneficial owner, negative sanctions-list screening report from a reputable compliance screening tool, corporate structural chart, and a legal opinion confirming that the entity has no transactions involving OFAC, EU, UN, or Samoa-sanctioned jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant inbound capital injection route for the Samoa IC is a SWIFT MT103 remittance from the parent company or founding shareholders to the tier-1 Samoa bank's USD or WST account. The remittance must include a purpose code indicating 'Overseas Direct Investment – Paid-Up Ordinary Share Capital' or 'Shareholder Subordinated Loan' on the SWIFT cover. The bank will require a letter from the IC's registered agent confirming the subscribed share capital, a copy of the board resolution approving the capital call, and a share subscription certificate. For the early-stage LegalTech SaaS entity, financial projections showing the shareholder loan being used exclusively for cloud infrastructure and software development are advisable. Funds received in USD are credited to a USD-denominated account and may be converted to WST for local operating expenses only where properly evidenced.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operational disbursements are cleared using SWIFT MT103 for low-value subscription payments, vendor payments, and recurring software licensing fees. For higher-risk legal outsourcing or technology services above USD 10,000, commercial banks may require a copy of the underlying contract and a proforma invoice, and might refer the payment to a documentary letter of credit where the trade route involves a non-OECD counterparty. Real-time gross settlement is only available domestically in WST; for USD/AUD cross-border flows, the Samoa bank uses its correspondent network in Australia or the United States (usually via BSP or ANZ's offshore head office), resulting in 1-3 business day execution. The IC should designate a single correspondent bank to minimise intermediary credits, and should encode its Samoa entity ID in the sending field 72 of the MT103 to avoid reconciliation delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (up to 12 months tenor) with a licensed Samoa commercial bank, subject to CBS dealer limits and documentary evidence of an underlying trade or subscription receivable.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing the WST against USD/AUD, executed with an offshore bank, since WST lacks robust onshore deliverable depth.

Currency Swaps for shareholder loan principal and interest repayments, limited to swaps between foreign currencies (e.g., USD/AUD) without crossing into WST if the original loan is denominated in a foreign currency.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (only with bank approval and full collateralisation, accepted for capital call and project financing, but not typically used for SaaS treasury operations due to simplicity and regulatory documentation cost).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual licence renewal fee for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) / Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a default penalty of approximately USD 120; continued non-payment beyond 60 days after the due date triggers administrative strike-off under the International Companies Act 1987.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation statement of registered agent, registered office and UBO details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission within the 30-day window attracts a late fee of USD 75; a further 90 days of non-compliance may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for Samoa International Companies; an audit is required only if shareholders holding at least 10% of voting rights notify the company in writing that they require one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework prescribed for International Companies; voluntary financial statements are commonly prepared in accordance with IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain and confirm up-to-date beneficial ownership information on an annual basis; any transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members and reported to the registered agent before the annual confirmation is signed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying International Company (IC) enjoys a territorial exemption for all non-Samoa-source income under the International Companies Act 1987 (ss.189-192). No capital gains tax, no stamp duty on share transfers, and no estate duty apply to the IC's offshore activities. If an IC conducts or derives income from Samoan domestic business, that portion is taxed at the resident corporate rate of 25% under the Income Tax Act 2015.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Return – Form AR-1 (International Companies Act 1987); submitted electronically through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Business Portal / e-Registry.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end, and within 15 months after incorporation for the first return; annual return must be filed every calendar year, regardless of the tax-exempt status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registration number, type of International Company, registered office and licensed registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name on the certificate of incorporation; use care to match English/Pinyin transliteration; state the offshore operational address only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential or service addresses, nationality and passport or ID details for each director and officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident natural persons are allowed; provide service-process addresses, not necessarily physical home addresses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, class and number of shares, and percentage holding for each shareholder; nominee details must be disclosed to the agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident may hold 100% of shares; beneficial owner details are filed with the registered agent but not publicly exposed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D – Business and Source Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement confirming that the IC has not carried on any business within Samoa and has no Samoa-source income, assets or employees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the IC is non-resident-owned and operates solely outside Samoa, select the exemption declaration; this field is critical to preserve the 0% tax status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the registered agent and director that the return is true and complete, with date and signature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A remote director may sign electronically through a SIFA-approved filing agent; the licenced Samoa agent countersigns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: WST 50 per month or part thereof, capped at WST 500; the Registrar may administratively strike off the IC after 3 months of default; reinstatement requires court order or payment of reinstatement fees. For continued default, the registered agent and directors may be jointly fined up to WST 1,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends paid by a non-resident-owned IC out of exempt offshore income; 15% on any distribution attributable to Samoan-source income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where Samoa has concluded a Double Taxation Arrangement, a non-resident recipient may file a treaty-relief application with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue using Form TR-1, attaching: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home jurisdiction, (ii) dividend/royalty/interest schedules, and (iii) a statement of beneficial ownership. SIFA simultaneously issues an IC Tax-Exemption Certificate and a Certificate of Residence. Relief is claimed at source before payment; if tax has already been withheld, a refund claim must be made within 4 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoan withholding tax on royalties and interest is 15% only where the source of the income is in Samoa. Foreign-source royalties and interest paid or received by an IC are subject to 0% withholding. Under an applicable DTA, the rate is commonly reduced to 0-10% depending on the treaty and type of payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory local transfer-pricing file applies to an exempt IC because it has no Samoan taxable income. If an IC acquires Samoan-source activity or becomes a taxable local person, the Income Tax Act 2015 Transfer Pricing Rules require a Local File where annual related-party cross-border transactions exceed WST 5,000,000 or the transaction value exceeds WST 1,000,000 per connected party.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime for International Companies; however, the International Companies Act 1987 and SIFA administrative practice require an IC to maintain a Samoan registered office, a licensed registered agent, and to refrain from domestic Samoan business. For foreign tax residency purposes, an IC must demonstrate substantive business through board minutes, commercial contracts, accounting records and bank accounts. Lack of substance may cause a parent jurisdiction to recharacterise the IC as a CFC or as resident in that parent jurisdiction. SIFA guidance also requires an annual economic substance declaration attached to the annual return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an International Company to disguise Samoan domestic business, fabricating an offshore presence, or knowingly submitting false declarations to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue or SIFA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2015, tax evasion attracts a penalty up to 200% of the tax shortfall, a criminal fine up to WST 100,000, and imprisonment up to 7 years. The court may order forfeiture of connected assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, registered agents and shadow officers are jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded tax; travel bans, asset restraining orders and director disqualification may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an IC solely to hold assets with no commercial substance, no business records, no board activity, and failure to file annual returns for more than 3 consecutive periods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may strike off the IC under the International Companies Act 1987; strike-off penalties up to WST 500 apply, and assets held by the struck-off company may be forfeited to the Crown unless restored by court order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for debts and obligations incurred after the striking-off if they knowingly continued trading; travel bans and personal fines up to WST 10,000 may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain an adequate register of beneficial owners, failure to report suspicious transactions, or allowing nominee arrangements to hide criminal proceeds in breach of the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A body corporate may be fined up to WST 1,000,000; natural persons may be imprisoned up to 10 years; the court may order civil asset forfeiture and cancellation of the company registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and beneficial owners may be criminally prosecuted where they knowingly permitted money laundering; personal civil restitution, travel bans, and professional disqualification are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly submitting false documents, forged signatures, or materially misleading information in the annual return, treaty relief application, or any SIFA filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act 1987, a person who makes a false statement or forges documents commits an offence punishable by a fine up to WST 50,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers and agents who sign or authorise fraudulent filings are personally liable for penalties, restitution of third-party losses, and may be disqualified from acting as company directors or registered agents.
